record.paper_title: Tree Spanners on Chordal Graphs: Complexity, Algorithms, Open Problems
record.context_brief: Chordal graphs of diameter at most t
record.original_question: For an integer t >= 3, what is the computational complexity of deciding whether a chordal graph G with diameter at most t admits a tree t-spanner, that is, a spanning tree preserving all graph distances up to multiplicative stretch t?

evidence.quote: What is the complexity of Tree t-Spanner

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G=(V,E) be a finite, simple, connected, undirected graph. The distance d_G(u,v) between two vertices u,v∈V is the number of edges on a shortest u–v path in G, and the diameter of G is max_{u,v∈V} d_G(u,v). A graph is chordal if every cycle of length at least 4 has a chord (an edge joining two non-consecutive vertices of the cycle). For an integer t≥1, a tree t-spanner of G is a spanning tree T of G such that d_T(u,v) ≤ t · d_G(u,v) for every pair of vertices u,v∈V; equivalently (for unweighted graphs), d_T(u,v) ≤ t whenever {u,v}∈E.

The Tree t-Spanner problem asks, given a graph G, whether G admits a tree t-spanner.

Problem. Fix an integer t≥3. Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem: given a chordal graph G of diameter at most t, decide whether G admits a tree t-spanner.
artifact.status_search_result: Known results show that for t≥4 Tree t-Spanner is NP-complete on chordal graphs of diameter at most t+1 (t even) or t+2 (t odd), and is solvable in linear time on chordal graphs of diameter at most t−1 (t even) or t−2 (t odd). The complexity of Tree 3-Spanner on chordal graphs remains open in general, and the boundary case of chordal graphs of diameter exactly t (the smallest unresolved diameter for each t≥3) is not resolved in the published literature.

status_evidence.title: Tree spanners on chordal graphs: complexity and algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: For any t≥4, Tree t-Spanner is NP-complete on chordal graphs of diameter at most t+1 (t even) or t+2 (t odd); chordal graphs of diameter ≤ t−1 (even t) or ≤ t−2 (odd t) admit a tree t-spanner constructible in linear time.
status_evidence.claim: The complexity gap for chordal graphs of diameter close to t is not closed; Tree 3-Spanner is open on chordal graphs.

status_evidence.title: A linear time algorithm for constructing tree 3-spanner in simple chordal bipartite graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Linear-time algorithm for tree 3-spanner in a restricted subclass; general chordal case unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses subclasses, indicating the general chordal-diameter-t question remains open.
